newsitem.title: CANADA: ICAO sees airline traffic growing 5.5 pct a year.
newsitem.headline: ICAO sees airline traffic growing 5.5 pct a year.

text.p: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) said on Wednesday that it expects world airline scheduled passenger traffic to grow at an average annual rate of 5.5 percent in the 1995-2005 period.
That compares with a 5.0 percent annual increase in traffic,measured as passenger-kilometers, over the 1985-1995 period, the Montreal-based United Nations agency said.
Total freight traffic growth in 1995-2005 is forecast to grow at 7.0 percent annually in terms of freight tonne-kilometers.

International traffic is expected to continue to grow faster than total traffic, at 7.0 percent annually in terms of passenger-kilometers and 7.5 percent annually in terms of freight tonne-kilometers.

Over the 1995-2005 period, the total number of domestic and international aircraft departures on scheduled services is forecast to rise by more than 25 percent and the total number of aircraft-kilometers flown is seen increasing by more than 50 percent, ICAO said.

The fastest growing international route groups for passenger traffic are forecast to be the TransPacific and Europe-Asia/Pacific, with the airlines of the Asia/Pacific region showing well above average growth in passenger and freight traffic.
